method: Read the full diff and all four new migration files end to end; re-measured several claims independently rather than trusting the ticket reports: (1) grepped the whole tree for CLR44 to check for a cross-lane errcode collision (#1114) -- none found outside the expected sites; (2) grepped for `is_active = false` across packages/db/migrations to check the #1078 AC1 claim that no chart-account deactivation exists -- confirmed zero matches; (3) counted `language plpgsql` / `search_path = clara` occurrences per migration to check SECURITY DEFINER + search_path discipline on every recut/new body across 0335-0338 -- all accounted for (0337's one-off count difference is a `language sql` function, also carrying search_path); (4) read 0338 section A in full to check the new relation's RLS posture -- FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set, only SELECT is granted to clara_authenticated, and clara_fn_owner's 'for all' policy is the house definer-path-owner escape hatch used since 0002, not an application grant; (5) diffed packages/db/package.json, packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs and packages/db/README.md against the fixed point to confirm the shared-file discipline (minimal hunk in migration order; only-additive README sections; no existing section edited); (6) walked every commit's `git show --stat` for all 28 commits to check for horizontal-slicing (a battery of red tests committed before any implementation) -- every commit pairs its migration edit with its test edit, confirming vertical slices; (7) spot-read the test files (prepayment-close-standing-instruction.test.mjs, prepayment-account-reservation.test.mjs, the amended prepayment-account-roster.test.mjs and prepayment-schedule-obo.test.mjs hunks, revenue-recognition.test.mjs, refusal-errcode-partition.test.mjs) for mocking of internal collaborators, tautological assertions and side-channel verification -- found none; the one direct-SQL-read seam (clara._acct_role_reserved via rootQuery in #1078's battery) is the shared reader body #1078 itself recuts, used alongside (not instead of) driving the three real claim doors, and matches the work order's allowance for a structural cell; (8) confirmed commit message format and the required Co-Authored-By trailer on all 28 commits; (9) confirmed no applied migration, no frozen-workflow manifest, no CONTEXT.md, no PRD/ARCHITECTURE file is touched by this diff.
overall_assessment: This lane's diff (26 files, +6943/-34, four new migrations 0335-0338) conforms to the repo's documented migration house law and to /tdd's vertical-slice discipline throughout. Every recut or new PL/pgSQL body carries SECURITY DEFINER and `set search_path = clara, pg_temp`; every prestate pin is stated as measured live on the lane database rather than copied from an older migration header (0338's own report explicitly warns the next implementer about this trap for `clara._adj_line_eligibility_breach`, and the pin it carries is in fact the live 0337 post-image, not 0317's); every migration's tail re-measures ACLs, payload byte-identity and (for 0338) RLS/CHECK posture off the live catalog rather than asserting intent. The one new relation (`clara.firm_standing_instructions`, 0338 SA) is created with `force row level security`, a SELECT-only grant to `clara_authenticated`, and no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant to any application or machine role -- the only mutation path is through the two SECURITY DEFINER doors. Shared files were touched minimally and at the documented sorted/append position (packages/db/package.json's $GATES list, packages/db/README.md's per-migration `## NNNN` sections, packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs's per-minted-name cohorts, apps/web/messages/en.json's single key). No applied migration, frozen-workflow manifest, PRD, ARCHITECTURE or CONTEXT.md entry was touched. Commit-by-commit history (28 commits, all with the required Co-Authored-By trailer) shows migration and test changed together in the same commit throughout every ticket, including the two multi-commit tickets (#1078's five feature slices plus two polish commits, #1050's six commits continuing a killed prior attempt) -- no battery of red tests precedes its implementation anywhere in the range, so the horizontal-slicing anti-pattern the work order names is not present. Test cells are driven through public doors (humanQuery/rootQuery-as-the-real-role, never a mocked internal collaborator), with independent literal expected values, and the handful of direct reads of an ungranted reader function are exactly the bodies the ticket itself recuts, used as a structural supplement to (not a replacement for) driving the real consuming doors -- consistent with the work order's carve-out for a catalog census / prestate pin / tail assertion. I found one labelled smell worth recording as a judgement call (below); nothing rises to a hard violation of a documented standard.

findings.title: Domain-to-release-door dispatch (prepayment vs staff_advance vs fa) is inlined three times in 0337 rather than named once
findings.evidence: Three separate PL/pgSQL bodies each re-derive, inline, which release door and which sentence corresponds to which reservation domain: `clara._fa_assert_code_unreserved` (§C, lines 416-424) does `case when v_domain = 'prepayment' then 'coa_account_prepayment_reserved' else 'coa_account_advance_reserved' end` for the machine reason token; `clara.upsert_fa_account_profile` (§D, lines 574-586) does `case when v_res_domain = 'prepayment' then 'retire that prepayment-account enrolment first (retire_prepayment_account...)' else 'retire that enrolment first (retire_staff_advance_account...)' end` for the human sentence; `clara._adv_enrolment_admission` (§E, ~lines 715-731) does the same dispatch again as an if/else producing near-identical prose (`v_advice := format('...retire_prepayment_account...')` vs `v_advice := format('...retire_staff_advance_account...')`). Before 0337 there were only two domains and no such dispatch existed in the pre-image (0041/0043 hardcoded a single remedy string each); 0337 is what introduces the three-way duplication, and the ticket's own follow-up 1 in its report (waveS-lane02-ticket1078.md, 'Follow-ups worth filing' #1) already names a fourth site (`clara._draft_opening_item_core`) that would need the identical case/if-else copied a fourth time.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a blocker: a small shared helper (e.g. `clara._reservation_release_advice(domain, ...)` returning the door name and/or the sentence fragment) would let §C, §D, §E and the eventual fourth site (follow-up 1) share one map instead of re-deriving the same domain dispatch, per the smell baseline's own fix ("replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share"). Not required for this lane to merge -- each of the three sites is independently tested and byte-pinned, and the duplication is currently only two-way per site (2-3 lines each), so the cost of centralizing now may not be worth the churn in an already-large migration. Worth doing the next time a domain is added, which the ticket's own follow-up already anticipates.
